intro: Lesson 16. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: أَرَءَيْتَ ٱلَّذِى يَنْهَىٰ (٩) عَبْدًا إِذَا صَلَّىٰٓ (١٠) أَرَءَيْتَ إِن كَانَ عَلَى ٱلْهُدَىٰٓ (١١) أَوْ أَمَرَ بِٱلتَّقْوَىٰٓ (١٢)

questions.q: Chunk and link Al-'Alaq 96:9-12 together, ayah by ayah.
questions.a: The class recites 96:9-12 together without the mushaf.

questions.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 96:9-12 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: Write one way you can help someone else to pray on time.
questions.a: For example: remind my brother kindly when it is time for Maghrib.

questions.q: Recite 96:1 to 12 to a partner. Count the izhar examples you hear.
Ayah 96:10 is about a servant of Allah who ...
questions.a: A) prays. 'A servant when he prays' (96:10). The other answers are not in the ayah.

questions.q: Al-'Alaq 96:11: «أَرَءَيْتَ إِن ...» Which word comes next?
Think again: Have you ever seen someone stop another person from doing something good? What should we do?
questions.a: Al-'Alaq 96:9 to 12 warns about someone who stops a servant of Allah from praying; we help others to do good.
